sentence: The applicant ___ (submit) the affidavit yesterday afternoon.

steps.step1_marker: Time marker identify hua: 'yesterday afternoon' — ye past ke ek definite aur completed point ko batata hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Aspect: Simple (past ka ek akela complete action bina kisi ongoing duration ya prior boundary ke).
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Affirmative Simple Past clause mein koi auxiliary verb nahi lagti; lexical verb V₂ form 'submitted' mein aati hai.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'The applicant submitted the affidavit yesterday afternoon.'

trapWarning: 'Has submitted' na likhein. Present connection ke bina definite past time markers Simple Past lete hain. (Agar past ke kisi specific point par ongoing action ho, toh Past Continuous lagta hai).

sentence: The Chief Justice ___ (preside) over the special constitutional bench currently.

steps.step1_marker: Time marker identify hua: 'currently' — ye batata hai ki action is waqt actively chal raha hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Aspect: Continuous (real-time mein chal raha progressive action).
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: 3rd-person singular subject ke saath auxiliary 'is' + lexical present participle V_ing 'presiding'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'The Chief Justice is presiding over the special constitutional bench currently.'

trapWarning: Simple Present ('presides') permanent routine batata hai, jabki 'currently' temporary dynamic state dikhata hai.

sentence: The IT team ___ (resolve) five critical database bugs already.

steps.step1_marker: Time marker identify hua: 'already' — ye aise complete action ko batata hai jiska present mein active connection hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Aspect: Perfect (present reference point se dekha gaya completed state).
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: Subject 'The IT team' yahan collective singular unit hai → auxiliary 'has' + lexical past participle V₃ 'resolved'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'The IT team has resolved five critical database bugs already.'

trapWarning: Present frame mein 'already' Present Perfect ('has resolved') ke saath aata hai. Beete huye definite time markers (jaise yesterday, ago) Simple Past lete hain.

sentence: He ___ (work) as a senior clerk in the High Court registry since 2018.

steps.step1_marker: Time marker identify hua: 'since 2018' — ye past ke starting point ko batata hai jo bina ruke present tak continue ho raha hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Aspect: Perfect Continuous (past se present tak faili hui duration).
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: Subject 'He' ke saath auxiliary 'has been' + lexical present participle V_ing 'working'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'He has been working as a senior clerk in the High Court registry since 2018.'

trapWarning: 'He is working since 2018' likhna galat hai; sirf continuous aspect 'since/for' duration nahi le sakta. Completed past period ke liye Simple Past lagta hai ('He worked in Jaipur for three years'), jabki present tak extend hone wale period ke liye Present Perfect ya Present Perfect Continuous lagta hai.

sentence: By 11 AM yesterday, the clerk ___ (dispatch) all official summons.

steps.step1_marker: Time marker identify hua: 'By 11 AM yesterday' — ye past ki ek specific deadline se pehle complete huye action ko batata hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Aspect: Perfect (past reference point se pehle ki completion).
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: Sabhi subjects ke saath past auxiliary 'had' + lexical past participle V₃ 'dispatched'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'By 11 AM yesterday, the clerk had dispatched all official summons.'

trapWarning: Past Perfect ('had + V₃') past reference point se pehle complete huye action ko dikhata hai. Do past actions ke beech cross-clause sequence of tenses Lesson 02 mein aayega.

sentence: By 5 PM this evening, the committee ___ (finalize) the technical merit list.

steps.step1_marker: Time marker identify hua: 'By 5 PM this evening' ('by + future deadline').
steps.step3_aspect: Aspect: Perfect (action future ki is boundary se pehle complete ho chuka hoga).
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: Future perfect auxiliaries 'will have' + lexical past participle V₃ 'finalized'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'By 5 PM this evening, the committee will have finalized the technical merit list.'

trapWarning: 'By + future time' future deadline se pehle completion dikhata hai, isliye Simple Future ('will finalize') ki jagah Future Perfect ('will have finalized') aayega.

sentence: At 4 PM yesterday, the system assistant ___ (verify) the server access records.

steps.step1_marker: Time marker identify hua: 'At 4 PM yesterday' — past ka ek precise instant jab action in progress tha.
steps.step3_aspect: Aspect: Continuous (us reference moment par chal raha progressive action).
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: Singular past auxiliary 'was' + lexical present participle V_ing 'verifying'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'At 4 PM yesterday, the system assistant was verifying the server access records.'

trapWarning: Sirf 'yesterday' dekh kar hamesha Simple Past mat lagayein. Jab past ke specific moment par koi action chal raha ho ('at 4 PM yesterday'), toh Past Continuous ('was verifying') lagta hai.

sentence: The judicial academy ___ (organize) specialized workshops every winter.

steps.step1_marker: Time marker identify hua: 'every winter' — regular annual routine ya habit ko show karta hai.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Subject 'The judicial academy' 3rd-person singular hai → base verb 'organize' mein '-s' jodenge → 'organizes' (affirmative simple present mein koi auxiliary nahi hoti).
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'The judicial academy organizes specialized workshops every winter.'

trapWarning: Scheduled institutional routine ('every winter') ke liye Simple Present ('organizes') use hota hai. Contextual exception: 'always' continuous ke saath annoyance dikhane ke liye use ho sakta hai ('He is always interrupting').

sentence: By next December, she ___ (serve) as judicial assistant for ten years.

steps.step1_marker: 'By next December' (future boundary) aur 'for ten years' (continuous duration) ka combination hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Aspect: Perfect Continuous (future ke kisi point tak measure ki gayi continuous duration).
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: Auxiliaries 'will have been' + lexical present participle V_ing 'serving'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'By next December, she will have been serving as judicial assistant for ten years.'

trapWarning: Future deadline ('by next December') aur ongoing duration ('for ten years') milkar Future Perfect Continuous banate hain.

sentence: He ___ not ___ (comprehend) the technical system guidelines at that time.

steps.step1_marker: Time marker identify hua: 'at that time' — definite past anchor.
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: Negative simple past mein auxiliary 'did' + 'not' + lexical base verb V₁ 'comprehend' aayega.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'He did not comprehend the technical system guidelines at that time.'

trapWarning: IMPORTANT AUXILIARY RULE: Negative aur interrogative Simple Past mein 'did' auxiliary verb hota hai jo past inflection carry karta hai; lexical main verb hamesha base form V₁ mein hona chahiye ('did not comprehend', 'did not comprehended' bilkul galat hai).

sentence: Look! The digital signature ___ (appear) on the portal now.

steps.step1_marker: Imperative cue 'Look!' + temporal marker 'now' — real-time mein ho rahe event par dhyan kheenchta hai.
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: Subject 'The digital signature' ke saath auxiliary 'is' + lexical present participle V_ing 'appearing'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'Look! The digital signature is appearing on the portal now.'

trapWarning: Attention attract karne wale exclamations ('Look!', 'Listen!', 'Hurry up!') ke saath Present Continuous use hota hai.

sentence: Prior to the 4 PM audit cutoff yesterday, the security team ___ (examine) the log files for two hours.

steps.step1_marker: Context check karein: past reference point ('Prior to the 4 PM audit cutoff yesterday') se pehle duration ('for two hours') accumulate ho rahi thi.
steps.step3_aspect: Aspect: Perfect Continuous (past reference time se pehle tak chalne wali duration).
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: Past perfect continuous auxiliary 'had been' + lexical present participle V_ing 'examining'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'Prior to the 4 PM audit cutoff yesterday, the security team had been examining the log files for two hours.'

trapWarning: Past reference point se theek pehle tak chalne wali duration ke liye Past Perfect Continuous ('had been examining') use hota hai. Cross-clause tense harmony Lesson 02 mein aayegi.

sentence: The advocate general ___ (address) the full bench at this exact time tomorrow.

steps.step1_marker: Marker identify hua: 'at this exact time tomorrow' — future ka ek specific ongoing moment.
steps.step3_aspect: Aspect: Continuous (future ke specific instant par chal raha action).
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: Future continuous auxiliaries 'will be' + lexical present participle V_ing 'addressing'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'The advocate general will be addressing the full bench at this exact time tomorrow.'

trapWarning: Akele 'tomorrow' ke saath Simple Future lagta hai, lekin 'at this time tomorrow' specific ongoing moment batata hai (Future Continuous).

sentence: Water ___ (freeze) at 0 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure.

steps.step1_marker: Universal scientific truth / natural law — jo past, present aur future sabhi mein barabar sach hai.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Uncountable noun 'Water' ke saath 3rd-person singular inflection '-s' lagega → 'freezes' (affirmative simple present mein koi auxiliary nahi hoti).
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius under standard atmospheric pressure.'

trapWarning: Scientific truths, universal laws aur permanent facts hamesha Simple Present ('freezes') mein rehte hain. Subordinate clauses mein inke retention ke rules Lesson 02 mein aayenge.

sentence: ___ the High Court administration ___ (publish) the provisional answer key yet?

steps.step1_marker: Interrogative sentence mein marker 'yet' identify hua — present tak action ke completion ke baare mein pooch raha hai.
steps.step4_inflection: Auxiliary aur Lexical verb: Interrogative inversion mein singular subject 'the High Court administration' se pehle auxiliary 'Has' aayegi, aur baad mein past participle V₃ 'published'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'Has the High Court administration published the provisional answer key yet?'

trapWarning: 'Yet' aamtaur par negative aur interrogative Present Perfect sentences mein contextual clue ki tarah kaam karta hai.
